doc.title: Lou Pallo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007

title: How Pallo met Les Paul and began Monday nights
summary: Les Paul showed up at Pallo's gigs, they jammed and recorded at his house, and began Monday nights at Fat Tuesday's about 23 years ago.

story.theme_name: Playing with Count Basie: joining, leading, leaving
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: How did the association with Les Paul come about?

Well that’s — we were talking about that — my best mentor was Tony Mattola and Les Paul. When Les Paul came out I said wow that’s, what a sound. Les lived in Mahwah, New Jersey and I’m in Pompton Lakes, New Jersey, which is like twelve miles difference, and after Les broke up with Mary he used to go out almost every night and I’d play five, six, seven nights a week — he would show up on all my gigs. That’s how I met him.

And then he says, “Come on over to the house,” so I went over to the house, we had a jam, we jammed together, and we would go out a lot. On whatever night I had off we would go out and that’s how I got to know him and play with him, then he put me on some recording sessions at his studio in his house. We did a lot of recording sessions there and he decided well let’s go out playing. And we picked up Monday nights at Fat Tuesday’s and that’s like 23 years ago. That’s a long time ago. And we’ve been playing every Monday night since then. And he won’t miss. He will not miss. It’s good therapy. © Fillius Jazz Archive -17-
Good therapy for everybody. And then he would come into the club where I’m playing and sit in with me three times a week.

People would see him and go, “Oh Les Paul’s going to be there tonight, let’s go.” And he would just sit and I would play songs like “Proud Mary” because that’s the type of place I was working in. Les would just play along with me. But of course now we’re doing his thing.
